interviews.why: The process's own interview: names the process, its sub-steps, gives the full scored impact grid, RTO >168 h, MTPD >168 h, BCMS relevance and the owner.

owner.name: Silke Jessen
owner.quote: It is a support process, and its process owner is the head of HR administration.

mtpd.speaker: Silke Jessen
mtpd.reason: Stated directly; consistent with her grid, which never reaches the intolerable level 4 at any horizon.

rto.quote: HR correspondence and document creation at Marschkamp has an RTO of more than 168 hours, because a short outage is classed as not critical for the organisation.
rto.speaker: Silke Jessen
rto.reason: The owner stated the RTO herself as more than 168 hours.

rpo.quote: Even with an outage of up to 168 hours, the process has no significant impact on health, finances, legal aspects, image or operations.
rpo.speaker: Silke Jessen
rpo.reason: Nothing was said about a recovery point; given the tolerance of a week-long outage, losing more than a week of correspondence is acceptable.

dependencies.heard: Effective workarounds exist to keep the correspondence going during an outage; no specific systems are named in the interview
dependencies.quote: There are effective workarounds to keep operations going.

conflicts.about: MTPD: the grid (2025) gives no MTPD within horizons by the method's rule, the draft says >168 h

sides.claim: no MTPD within horizons (the method's rule over the grid, 2025)
sides.speaker: method

conflicts.why: The method derives the MTPD from the grid; the other figure is the thing to explain.

gaps.what: The interview names no IT systems or documents the correspondence depends on (e.g. Microsoft 365, SharePoint, personnel file systems), so dependencies and RPO could not be tied to register assets.
gaps.ask: Which systems and records does HR correspondence run on, and how much of issued/filed correspondence may be lost (RPO)?
